FINAL_STATES: u2
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:

(u0, blocker_moved & has_door_key) -> u2
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, has_door_key) -> u2
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, else) -> u2

(u0, blocker_moved & !has_door_key, u1) -> 0.1

(u1, has_door_key, u2) -> 0.9
feedback: The RM is a faithful encoding of the response property 'after the ball has been moved away from the door, the key must be held at that point or at some later point'. State semantics are correct: u0 = ball not yet moved, u1 = ball moved with the obligation pending, u2 = key held after the move (absorbing final). Ordering is handled correctly: in u0, has_door_key alone falls through to the else self-loop, so acquiring the key before moving the ball does not satisfy the task, and the agent must hold it at or after the move (u1 -> u2). The absence of regressions is right for this task: 'has been moved' is event-like (perfect aspect), so dropping the ball back in front of the door does not discharge the obligation; u1 correctly persists until has_door_key, and u2 correctly stays absorbing once satisfied. Irrelevant propositions (key_lost, door_open, target_picked_up) and all other label combinations are covered by per-state else self-loops in u0, u1, and u2. Guards are predicate-only (propositions with & and !, no raw actions). Rewards are dense but bounded and path-consistent: 0.1 for moving the blocker, 0.9 for the key afterwards, total 1.0 equal to the direct-entry reward; each progress transition fires at most once, no negative or unbounded rewards, and reward entries are keyed by (state, guard, next state) with guards matching the transition function. Format matches the paper exactly (REWARD_MACHINE / STATES / INITIAL_STATE / FINAL_STATES / TRANSITION_FUNCTION / REWARD_FUNCTION); FINAL_STATES: u2 is nonempty, declared in STATES, and accepting. Soundness and completeness hold: the first step on which blocker_moved turns true is the ball pick-up step, so the agent's hands hold the ball and has_door_key is false there, sending u0 -> u1; any later step carrying the key fires u1 -> u2, so every satisfying trace reaches u2, and u2 is reachable (pick up ball, drop it away from the door, pick up the key). One non-blocking note: the guard (u0, blocker_moved & has_door_key) -> u2 is environmentally unreachable for the reason above (blocker_moved and has_door_key can never both be true while still in u0, since the first blocker_moved step has the ball in hand); it harmlessly encodes the 'at that point' clause of the task and does not affect state reachability or reward consistency, but the live path u0 -> u1 -> u2 alone already covers all satisfying behaviors.

feedback: All five environment-declared propositions are implemented exactly, with no extra functions and none missing. (1) blocker_moved: the scan finds the door and checks its left-adjacent cell for a ball, which is equivalent to the canonical expression over (dx-1, dy) since there is exactly one door and the ball starts at (dx-1, dy); it is non-latching (re-false if the ball is dropped back there) and counts a carried ball as moved. Short-circuit evaluation means env.grid.get(x-1, y) is only reached when a door is found, and boundary cells at x=0 are walls, so no out-of-bounds access occurs. (2) has_door_key, (3) door_open, and (4) target_picked_up match the documented expressions verbatim: key color matched against the door color, door openness via is_open, and mission string f'pick up the {color} box'. (5) key_lost is a correct one-step event: prev['has_door_key'] (read-only complete previous valuation, guarded for absence) and not K and not D with K and D inlined identically to the persistent predicates; it fires only on the single step after the key is dropped while the door is closed, matching the seed-0 trace where the step-19 drop with the door open keeps it false. The constraints (door_open after blocker_moved and has_door_key; target_picked_up after door_open; mutual exclusions involving key_lost) all follow from these faithful definitions plus environment mechanics. Code is syntactically valid, uses only the documented API (env.grid.get, env.carrying, env.mission, env.width, env.height, env.episode_memory), performs no imports, actions, or mutations, and returns booleans from all predicates. Unused-in-RM predicates door_open, target_picked_up, and key_lost are correctly present as required.
